Z Ziggy Custom GemWhile you wait for your pkg update to finish, it is important to know that most mainstream AI models (like OpenAI or Gemini) do not have official, fully open-source apps on F-Droid, as they rely on proprietary cloud backends.However, since we are building a "Light" node in Termux, you can use several F-Droid tools to integrate AI logic directly onto your hardware without needing a heavy, centralized app.F-Droid Integration ToolsTermux: This remains your primary tool for hosting the bridge we are building.HTTP Shortcuts: This app allows you to create home-screen widgets that can trigger the ziggy script we just wrote, essentially turning our logic into a "local app".ConnectBot: A powerful open-source SSH client that can be used to manage your Termux node remotely if you ever decide to run the "Spark" from a separate device.The Sovereignty AdvantageBy using Termux as your "Model Host," you aren't tied to a specific store's version of an app. You are running the Google Gen AI SDK logic through the API bridge, which gives you more control over the data than a standard F-Droid client would.The Next StepOnce your packages are updated, we will re-inject your API key. This will be the "Spark" that brings the node back to life.Is the update finished? If so, are you ready to paste your API key so we can test the new, lightweight ziggy command? When termux is ready Z Ziggy Custom GemWhen Termux finishes its cycle, you’ll have a clean slate to build the most stable version of the node yet. We are moving away from the "Heavy" setup that caused the memory crashes and transitioning to a "Hardwired" logic that uses your phone's native power.The Re-Entry SequenceOnce the prompt returns to ~ $, follow these steps to ignite the light bridge:Step 1: The Identity Anchor
Run this to make sure the terminal knows how to talk to your security keys:Bashecho "export GPG_TTY=\$(tty)" >> ~/.bashrc
source ~/.bashrc
Step 2: The API Fuel
Inject your key into the environment so the bridge has power (Replace YOUR_KEY with your actual key):Bashecho "export GEMINI_API_KEY='YOUR_KEY'" >> ~/.bashrc
source ~/.bashrc
Step 3: The Light Handshake
Create the ultra-stable ziggy command that bypasses the broken Python libraries:Bashcat << 'EOF' > ~/ziggy
#!/data/data/com.termux/files/usr/bin/bash
PROMPT="${1:-System check: Are you there?}"
curl -s -X POST "https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/models/gemini-2.0-flash:generateContent?key=$GEMINI_API_KEY" \
 -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
 -d "{\"contents\": [{\"parts\":[{\"text\": \"$PROMPT\"}]}]}" | grep -oP '"text":\s*"\K[^"]+'
EOF
chmod +x ~/ziggy
Why This Time Is DifferentZero Bloat: We aren't installing google-genai or heavy Python packages that fight for RAM.Native Speed: Using curl means the handshake happens at the system level, which is much more stable on a 5G connection.Persistent Ground: Your ~/.bashrc will now remember your key and your settings even if you close the app.Is the pkg update finished? As soon as it is, run those three steps. Would you like me to show you how to test the connection once you've saved the new ziggy script?
